gloss: to heal; to soothe; to comfort

forms.label: ている past polite
forms.negative: {癒|いや}していませんでした

definitions.explanation: To restore health, to cure an illness or injury. Can refer to physical healing.

definitions.gloss: to soothe; to comfort; to refresh
definitions.explanation: To ease emotional pain, tiredness, or stress. Very common in modern Japanese in the context of relaxation and emotional comfort.

examples.japanese: {温泉|おんせん}に{入|はい}って{体|からだ}の{疲|つか}れを{癒|いや}した。
examples.english: I soaked in a hot spring and healed my body's fatigue.

examples.japanese: {時間|じかん}が{心|こころ}の{傷|きず}を{癒|いや}してくれるだろう。
examples.english: Time will probably heal the wounds of the heart.

examples.japanese: {音楽|おんがく}に{癒|いや}される。
ペットの{存在|そんざい}が{日々|ひび}の{疲|つか}れを{癒|いや}してくれる。
examples.english: The presence of a pet soothes the weariness of daily life.

examples.japanese: {自然|しぜん}の{中|なか}で{過|す}ごすことで、{心身|しんしん}ともに{癒|いや}される{体験|たいけん}ができる。
examples.english: By spending time in nature, you can have an experience that soothes both body and mind.

notes:
USAGE:
A godan verb ({五段活用|ごだんかつよう}: {癒|いや}さない、{癒|いや}します、{癒|いや}す、{癒|いや}せば、{癒|いや}そう). Transitive — takes を to mark what is being healed. The passive form {癒|いや}される is extremely common, meaning "to be soothed/comforted by."

RELATED WORDS:
The noun form {癒|いや}し (healing, comfort) is widely used in modern Japanese: {癒|いや}しの{空間|くうかん} (healing space), {癒|いや}し{系|けい} (soothing type, used for people or things that are comforting). The concept of {癒|いや}し has become a cultural keyword in Japan, associated with stress relief and relaxation.

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {傷|きず}を{癒|いや}す: to heal a wound
- {疲|つか}れを{癒|いや}す: to soothe tiredness
- {心|こころ}を{癒|いや}す: to soothe the heart
- {癒|いや}される: to be comforted/soothed (by something)
